record.what_it_does: Open-source CLI and Node library that renders Mermaid diagram text to SVG, PNG or PDF.
record.auth_notes: There is no hosted service and no authentication. The tool runs locally through npm (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli), Docker or Podman. Mermaid Chart's hosted MCP is a separate commercial product and uses its own auth: OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration, or a Mermaid token. That auth does not apply to mermaid-cli.
record.access_notes: The tool is MIT-licensed and free to install from npm or Docker. It has no hosted API, accounts or credentials, so there is nothing to gate.
record.api_breadth_notes: There is no network API. The only interface is local: the `mmdc` CLI plus a Node `run` function, which the README says is not covered by semver. Its one job is to render a Mermaid definition, or the Mermaid blocks in a Markdown file, to SVG, PNG or PDF.
record.mcp_notes: The mermaid-js GitHub org has 14 repos and none of them is an MCP server. Community servers wrap or reimplement rendering: @peng-shawn/mermaid-mcp-server, mcp-mermaid (hustcc) and mermaid-render-mcp, which uses @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli. Separately, Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai), the commercial company behind Mermaid, runs an official remote MCP at https://mcp.mermaid.ai/mcp and /sse. It has 9 tools for validation, rendering and project/diagram CRUD, and needs a Mermaid account. The Stacklok "Official" listing points to that server's docs. It belongs to the Mermaid Chart product, not to mermaid-cli.
record.blocker_notes: This is a local CLI with no hosted API or user accounts. Composio could only self-host the renderer (headless Chromium via Puppeteer) as a utility, which would not be an authenticated integration. If the goal is "Mermaid" as a service, the buildable target is Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai): it has an official remote MCP with OAuth 2.1 and a free Basic tier. That is a different product from this hint.

evidence.quote: It takes a mermaid definition file as input and generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file as output.
Please be aware that the NodeJS API is not covered by semver, as mermaid-cli follows mermaid's versioning.
mermaid-cli: Command line tool for the Mermaid library
